questions.prompt: How many hours do you usually sleep?
questions.sampleA1: I sleep six hours. I am tired. I want more sleep.
questions.sampleA2: I sleep seven hours. But I want to sleep more. Because I like sleep.
questions.sampleB1: I usually sleep for about seven hours. For example, last night I slept from 11pm to 6am. However, sometimes I sleep less if I am busy. I try to get enough sleep. It is important for my health.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I usually get around seven or eight hours a night, which seems to be my sweet spot. On a good day I'll be in bed by eleven and up by seven. That said, if I've got a deadline, I sometimes burn the midnight oil and end up shattered the next morning, so I try to catch up on sleep at the weekend.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men olti soat uxlayman. Men charchaganman. Men ko'proq uxlashni xohlayman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men yetti soat uxlayman. Lekin men ko'proq uxlashni xohlayman. Chunki men uxlashni yaxshi ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB1: Men odatda taxminan yetti soat uxlayman. Masalan, o'tgan kecha men soat 23:00 dan ertalabki 6:00 gacha uxladim. Biroq, ba'zan band bo'lsam, kamroq uxlayman. Men yetarli uxlashga harakat qilaman. Bu mening sog'lig'im uchun muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men odatda har kecha yetti-sakkiz soat atrofida uxlashga harakat qilaman. Umuman olganda, bu miqdor menga kun davomida dam olgan va unumli his qilishimga imkon beradi. Albatta, ish yoki boshqa majburiyatlar tufayli bu maqsadga erisha olmaydigan vaqtlar ham bo'ladi. Shunga qaramay, men har doim imkon qadar uyquni to'ldirishga harakat qilaman, chunki uning umumiy farovonlik uchun ahamiyatini tushunaman.

vocabulary.title: How many - Hours
idioms: lose sleep over something - "biror narsa haqida qayg'urib uxlay olmaslik"
sentenceStarters: "I usually sleep..." - "Men odatda uxlayman..."
"On average, I get..." - "O'rtacha, men olaman..."
"I aim for... hours of sleep." - "Men ... soat uxlashga harakat qilaman."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Well, on average, I aim for around seven to eight hours of sleep a night. I've found that hitting that sweet spot really makes a difference in my overall mood and productivity. Ideally, I'd love to get nine hours, but realistically, life often gets in the way.

If I consistently get less than seven hours, I start to feel it pretty quickly – my concentration wavers, and I'm more prone to irritability. I'm a firm believer that sleep is one of the cornerstones of good health, and I really try to prioritize it, even when things get hectic. Plus, I've noticed that burning the candle at both ends just leads to diminishing returns in the long run.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Xo'sh, o'rtacha hisobda, men har kecha yetti-sakkiz soat atrofida uxlashga harakat qilaman. Men shuni aniqladimki, shu maqbul miqdorga erishish mening umumiy kayfiyatim va unumdorligimga katta ta'sir ko'rsatadi. Ideal holda, men to'qqiz soat uxlashni xohlardim, lekin real hayotda ko'pincha turli xil ishlar xalaqit beradi.

Agar men doimiy ravishda yetti soatdan kamroq uxlasam, buni tezda his qila boshlayman – diqqatim susayadi va men tez asabiylashadigan bo'lib qolaman. Men uyqu yaxshi sog'liqning asosiy omillaridan biri ekanligiga qat'iy ishonaman va ishlar tig'iz bo'lganda ham, unga ustuvor ahamiyat berishga harakat qilaman. Qolaversa, men shuni payqadimki, tinimsiz ishlash oxir-oqibatda hech qanday foyda bermaydi.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer taking photos or appearing in photos?
questions.sampleA1: I like taking photos. I don't like being in photos. It is fun.
questions.sampleA2: I like taking photos. Because it is fun. But I don't like being in them very much.
questions.sampleB1: I prefer taking photos. I don't like being in them. For example, I like to take pictures of nature. However, I sometimes take selfies with my friends. But I prefer to take photos of other things.
questions.sampleB2: I'd say I'm much happier behind the camera than in front of it. The thing is, I really enjoy capturing a moment and playing around with angles and lighting. To be honest, I get a bit camera-shy when someone points a lens at me, so I'd rather be the one calling the shots. It just feels more me.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men suratga olishni yaxshi ko'raman. Suratda bo'lishni yoqtirmayman. Bu qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men suratga olishni yaxshi ko'raman. Chunki bu qiziqarli. Lekin men suratda bo'lishni unchalik yoqtirmayman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men suratga olishni afzal ko'raman. Suratda bo'lishni yoqtirmayman.
Masalan, men tabiatning suratlarini olishni yaxshi ko'raman.
Biroq, ba'zan do'stlarim bilan selfi tushaman. Lekin men boshqa narsalarni suratga olishni afzal ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men suratga tushishdan ko'ra suratga olishni afzal ko'raman, deb ayta olaman.
Asosan, men ob'ektiv ortida bo'lish bilan keladigan ijodiy nazoratdan zavqlanaman. Men lahzalarni suratga olishni va uzoq muddatli xotiralarni yaratishni yoqtiraman. Ba'zan suratga tushishga qarshi bo'lmasam-da, tajribani hujjatlashtiradigan odam bo'lish menga ko'proq zavq beradi. Bu menga maqsad hissini beradi va o'z badiiy tomonimni ifoda etishga imkon beradi.

vocabulary.title: Do you - photos
idioms: a picture is worth a thousand words - "bir rasm ming so'zga arziydi"
sentenceStarters: "I prefer..." - "Men afzal ko'raman..."
"I like... more than..." - "Menga ... ...dan ko'ra ko'proq yoqadi..."
"I enjoy..." - "Men zavqlanaman..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
That's an interesting question! I think I lean towards preferring to take photos rather than being in them. To me, photography is a creative outlet. I enjoy capturing moments and seeing the world through a lens. Moreover, I find it creatively fulfilling to frame a shot and play with composition and lighting. It's a way to express myself without necessarily being the subject of attention.

Having said that, I don't mind being in photos occasionally, especially if it's with friends and family. But generally speaking, I'm more comfortable behind the camera. I guess I just prefer to be the observer rather than the observed. It also helps that I’m pretty good at taking photos and not so much at posing for them! Each to their own, I suppose.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu qiziqarli savol! Menimcha, suratga tushishdan ko'ra, suratga olishni afzal ko'raman. Men uchun fotosurat ijodiy chiqish yo'li. Men lahzalarni suratga olishdan va dunyoni linza orqali ko'rishdan zavqlanaman. Bundan tashqari, kadrlarni tuzish va kompozitsiya va yorug'lik bilan o'ynash menga ijodiy jihatdan zavq beradi. Bu o'zimni diqqat markazida bo'lmasdan turib ifoda etish usuli.

Shuni aytishim kerakki, vaqti-vaqti bilan, ayniqsa do'stlar va oila bilan bo'lsam, suratga tushishga qarshi emasman. Ammo umuman olganda, men kamera orqasida o'zimni qulayroq his qilaman. Menimcha, men kuzatuvchi bo'lishni kuzatiluvchi bo'lishdan afzal ko'raman. Bundan tashqari, suratga olishda ancha yaxshiman, suratga tushish uchun poza olishda esa unchalik emasman! Har kimning o'z didi bor, deb o'ylayman.

questions.sampleA1: Yes, I like parks. Parks are nice. I go to the park.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like visiting parks. Because they are green and quiet. I can relax in the park.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I like visiting parks very much. For example, I often go to the park on weekends. I like to walk and read a book there. However, sometimes the park is crowded. But I still enjoy visiting parks.
questions.sampleB2: Yeah, absolutely — I'm a big fan of parks. Whenever things get on top of me, a stroll through the park really helps me unwind and clear my head. The thing is, you get a proper breath of fresh air away from all the traffic and noise. I suppose it's my go-to place to recharge my batteries at the weekend.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha, menga parklar yoqadi. Parklar yaxshi. Men parkga boraman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men bog‘larga borishni yaxshi ko‘raman. Chunki ular yashil va sokin. Men bog‘da dam olishim mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men bog‘larga borishni juda yaxshi ko‘raman.
Masalan, men ko‘pincha dam olish kunlari bog‘ga boraman. U yerda sayr qilishni va kitob o‘qishni yaxshi ko‘raman.
Biroq, ba’zan bog‘ odamlar bilan gavjum bo‘ladi. Lekin men baribir bog‘larga borishdan zavqlanaman.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Ha, men parklarga borishni albatta yoqtiraman. Ular kundalik hayotning stresslaridan juda zarur bo'lgan dam olishni ta'minlaydi.
Birinchidan, men tabiat bilan o'ralash imkoniyatini qadrlayman. Toza havo va yashil maydonlar juda tetiklantiradi.
Bundan tashqari, parklar ko'pincha piyoda yo'laklari, piknik joylari va o'yin maydonchalari kabi turli xil tadbirlarni taklif etadi, bu ularni do'stlar va oila bilan vaqt o'tkazish uchun ajoyib joyga aylantiradi.
Umuman olganda, men parklarga borishni juda foydali va yoqimli tajriba deb bilaman.

vocabulary.title: Do you - parks
idioms: stop and smell the roses - "to'xtab atirgul hidini his qilmoq"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I like..." - "Ha, menga yoqadi..."
"I enjoy visiting..." - "Men ...ga tashrif buyurishdan zavqlanaman..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Absolutely, I do! I'm quite fond of visiting parks. They offer a wonderful escape from the hustle and bustle of city life. Firstly, I appreciate the opportunity to connect with nature, even in an urban setting. The greenery, fresh air, and sounds of birds chirping help me unwind and feel more relaxed. It’s a great way to clear my head. Parks are also great places for exercise.

Furthermore, parks often serve as community hubs, where people can gather, socialize, and participate in recreational activities. In essence, parks provide a valuable space for both individual reflection and social interaction. I think a change is as good as a rest, and a visit to the park certainly provides that.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Albatta, yoqtiraman! Men parklarga borishni juda yaxshi ko'raman. Ular shahar hayotining shovqinidan ajoyib qochish imkoniyatini beradi. Birinchidan, men hatto shahar sharoitida ham tabiat bilan bog'lanish imkoniyatini qadrlayman. Ko'katlar, toza havo va qushlarning sayrashi menga dam olishga va o'zimni xotirjam his qilishga yordam beradi. Bu fikrlarni jamlashning ajoyib usuli. Parklar, shuningdek, mashq qilish uchun ajoyib joylardir.

Bundan tashqari, parklar ko'pincha odamlar yig'iladigan, muloqot qiladigan va dam olish tadbirlarida ishtirok etadigan jamoat markazlari vazifasini bajaradi. Aslida, parklar ham shaxsiy mulohaza, ham ijtimoiy muloqot uchun qimmatli joyni ta'minlaydi. O'zgarish dam olish bilan barobar deb o'ylayman va parkga tashrif aynan shuni ta'minlaydi.

questions.prompt: What ways of expressing personal thoughts are shown in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1: One person writes. One person uses computer. They are thinking.
questions.sampleA2: One person writes in a diary. And one person is on the computer. They are sharing their ideas.
questions.sampleB1: The first picture shows someone writing in a diary. The second picture shows someone using social media. For example, the diary is private. However, social media is public. Both are ways to express thoughts.
questions.sampleB2: Well, both pictures show different ways of getting your thoughts out there. In the first one, someone's posting on social media or writing a blog, so they're sharing their feelings openly with a wide audience and probably fishing for feedback. In the second, a person's writing in a diary late at night, which is far more private and personal. To my mind, the big contrast is public versus private — one puts everything out in the open, while the other keeps it strictly under wraps, for their eyes only.
questions.uzSampleA1: Bir kishi yozmoqda. Bir kishi kompyuterdan foydalanmoqda. Ular o'ylashmoqda.
questions.uzSampleA2: Bir kishi kundalikka yozmoqda. Va bir kishi kompyuterda. Ular o'z fikrlari bilan bo'lishmoqda.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Birinchi rasmda kundalik daftariga yozayotgan odam ko'rsatilgan. Ikkinchi rasmda esa ijtimoiy tarmoqlardan foydalanayotgan odam ko'rsatilgan.
Masalan, kundalik daftar shaxsiy hisoblanadi.
Biroq, ijtimoiy tarmoqlar ommaviy. Ikkalasi ham fikrlarni ifoda etish usullaridir.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Rasmlarda shaxsiy fikrlarni ifodalashning ikki xil usuli ko'rsatilgan. Birinchi rasmda kundalik yozayotgan odam tasvirlangan bo'lib, bu shaxsiy va o'ychan yondashuvni anglatadi. Bu tashqi baholash bosimisiz, filtrlarsiz o'zini ifoda etishga imkon beradi.
Aksincha, ikkinchi rasmda ijtimoiy tarmoqlarda post joylashtirayotgan odam tasvirlangan bo'lib, bu ommaviy va tashqi tomonga yo'naltirilgan yondashuvni ifodalaydi. Bu darhol fikr-mulohazalarni olish va boshqalar bilan aloqa qilish imkonini beradi, lekin u o'z fikrlarini kengroq auditoriyaga va potentsial tanqidlarga ham oshkor qiladi. Ikkala usul ham shaxsiy ifoda uchun vosita bo'lib xizmat qiladi, turli xil xohishlar va qulaylik darajalariga mos keladi.

vocabulary.title: What ways - pictures?
idioms: a penny for your thoughts - "nima haqida o'ylayapsiz?"
sentenceStarters: "The pictures show..." - "Rasmlar ko'rsatadi..."
"One image depicts..." - "Bir rasmda tasvirlangan..."
"The images illustrate..." - "Rasmlar tasvirlaydi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
The pictures illustrate different ways of expressing personal thoughts. The first image shows someone writing in a diary, which represents a private and introspective form of expression. It's a way to sort through one's feelings and thoughts in a personal and confidential space. This method allows for unfiltered honesty and self-reflection, without the pressure of external judgment. Essentially, it's a conversation with oneself.

The second image depicts someone posting on social media, which is a public and extroverted form of expression. It involves sharing thoughts and feelings with a wide audience, seeking validation, and engaging in dialogue. This method allows for instant feedback and connection with others who may share similar viewpoints. However, it also comes with the risk of criticism and exposure. Ultimately, both methods serve the same purpose – to articulate and share one's inner world – but they cater to different personalities and preferences. Different strokes for different folks, I suppose. Both allow you to get something off your chest.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rasmlarda shaxsiy fikrlarni ifoda etishning turli usullari tasvirlangan. Birinchi rasmda kundalikka yozayotgan odam ko'rsatilgan, bu shaxsiy va ichki fikrlash shaklini ifodalaydi. Bu shaxsiy va maxfiy makonda o'z his-tuyg'ulari va fikrlarini tartibga solish usuli. Bu usul tashqi baholash bosimisiz, filtrlarsiz halollik va o'z-o'zini tahlil qilish imkonini beradi. Aslida, bu o'z-o'zi bilan suhbat.

Ikkinchi rasmda ijtimoiy tarmoqlarda post joylashtirayotgan odam tasvirlangan, bu ommaviy va tashqi fikrlash shaklidir. Bu fikrlar va his-tuyg'ularni keng auditoriya bilan baham ko'rish, tasdiqlashni izlash va muloqotga kirishishni o'z ichiga oladi. Bu usul o'xshash nuqtai nazarga ega bo'lgan boshqalar bilan tezkor fikr-mulohazalar va aloqa o'rnatish imkonini beradi. Biroq, bu tanqid va oshkoralik xavfini ham o'z ichiga oladi. Oxir oqibat, ikkala usul ham bir xil maqsadga xizmat qiladi – o'z ichki dunyosini ifodalash va baham ko'rish – lekin ular turli xil shaxsiyatlar va afzalliklarga mos keladi. Har kimning o'z didi bor, deb o'ylayman. Ikkalasi ham sizga dardingizni aytishga imkon beradi.

questions.prompt: Why do some people prefer keeping their thoughts private?
questions.sampleA1: Some people no talk. They like quiet. It is their way.
questions.sampleA2: Some people like to keep secrets. They do not tell everyone. It is because they are shy and it is okay.
questions.sampleB1: Some people don't like to share their thoughts. For example, they might be afraid of what others will think. However, sometimes it's good to talk to someone. It can help you feel better. But it is also okay to keep things private if you want to.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I suppose some people are just naturally private and like to keep things to themselves. The thing is, opening up can leave you feeling exposed, and not everyone wants to be judged or have their words twisted. On top of that, with social media everywhere these days, a lot of folk are wary of oversharing, so they play their cards close to their chest.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ba'zi odamlar gapirmaydi. Ular sokinlikni yaxshi ko'radi. Bu ularning yo'li.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ba'zi odamlar sir saqlashni yaxshi ko'radilar. Ular hamma bilan gaplashmaydilar. Buning sababi ular uyatchan va bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ba'zi odamlar o'z fikrlarini baham ko'rishni yoqtirmaydi.
Masalan, ular boshqalar nima deb o'ylashidan qo'rqishlari mumkin.
Biroq, ba'zida kimdir bilan gaplashish yaxshi. Bu sizning o'zingizni yaxshi his qilishingizga yordam berishi mumkin. Lekin agar xohlasangiz, narsalarni shaxsiy saqlash ham yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Ko'p odamlar o'z fikrlarini yashirishni turli sabablarga ko'ra afzal ko'rishadi.
Birinchidan, ular boshqalarning hukmidan yoki salbiy reaksiyalaridan qo'rqishlari mumkin.
Ikkinchidan, ular shunchaki introvertroq bo'lishi va narsalarni ichki tomondan qayta ishlashni afzal ko'rishlari mumkin.
Bundan tashqari, shaxsiy hayotga oid xavotirlar bugungi raqamli davrda tobora muhim ahamiyat kasb etmoqda. Odamlar haddan tashqari ko'p narsalarni baham ko'rishning potentsial xavflaridan ko'proq xabardor va ular nimalarni oshkor qilishlari haqida ehtiyotkor bo'lishni tanlashlari mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Why do...
idioms: keep something close to your chest - "sir saqlash"
play your cards close to your chest - "sirini ochmaslik"
sentenceStarters: "I think the reason is..." - "Menimcha, sababi..."
"It could be due to..." - "Buning sababi... bo'lishi mumkin"
"One possible explanation is..." - "Buning bir mumkin bo'lgan izohi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Well, I think there are several reasons why some individuals clam up and prefer to keep their thoughts to themselves. Firstly, there's the fear of vulnerability. Sharing your innermost thoughts can feel like exposing a part of yourself, and not everyone is comfortable with that level of openness. They might be worried about being judged, misunderstood, or even ridiculed. Secondly, some people are naturally more introverted and reflective. They process their thoughts internally and don't feel the need to verbalize them to feel validated.

Furthermore, privacy concerns are increasingly relevant in today's world. With the prevalence of social media and data collection, people are more aware of the potential consequences of sharing their thoughts publicly. They might be concerned about their thoughts being taken out of context, used against them, or simply becoming part of the digital noise. It's a case of once bitten, twice shy. So, it's not always about being secretive, but rather about being discerning about who you share with and why.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Xo'sh, menimcha, ba'zi odamlar nima uchun o'z fikrlarini yashirishni va o'zlarida saqlashni afzal ko'rishlarining bir nechta sabablari bor. Birinchidan, zaif bo'lib qolishdan qo'rqish bor. Eng ichki fikrlaringizni baham ko'rish o'zingizning bir qismini ochib tashlagandek tuyulishi mumkin va hamma ham bunday ochiqlik darajasidan mamnun emas. Ular hukm qilinishdan, noto'g'ri tushunilishdan yoki hatto masxara qilinishdan xavotirda bo'lishlari mumkin. Ikkinchidan, ba'zi odamlar tabiatan ko'proq introvert va mulohazali bo'lishadi. Ular o'z fikrlarini ichki tomondan qayta ishlaydilar va o'zlarini tasdiqlash uchun ularni og'zaki ifodalashga hojat sezmaydilar.

Bundan tashqari, shaxsiy hayotga oid xavotirlar bugungi kunda tobora dolzarb bo'lib bormoqda. Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar va ma'lumotlar yig'ishning keng tarqalishi bilan odamlar o'z fikrlarini ommaga e'lon qilishning potentsial oqibatlaridan ko'proq xabardor bo'lishmoqda. Ular o'z fikrlari kontekstdan uzib olinishi, ularga qarshi ishlatilishi yoki shunchaki raqamli shovqinning bir qismiga aylanishidan xavotirda bo'lishlari mumkin. Bir marta chaqsa, ikki marta ehtiyot bo'lish holati. Shunday ekan, gap har doim sir saqlashda emas, balki kim bilan va nima uchun baham ko'rishda farosatli bo'lishdadir.

questions.prompt: How has social media changed the way people share their feelings?
questions.sampleA1: Social media is different now. People share feelings. It is online.
questions.sampleA2: Social media is new. People can share feelings online and show pictures. But sometimes it is not real.
questions.sampleB1: Social media has changed how people share feelings. For example, people post happy pictures to show they are doing well. However, sometimes they are not really happy. It can make other people feel bad about themselves. It's important to remember that social media is not always real life.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, it's changed the game. On the one hand, people can now share how they feel instantly with hundreds of followers. But on the other hand, a lot of it is a highlight reel — everyone paints a rosy picture and only shows the good bits. So it's a double-edged sword: it brings us together but piles on the pressure to look perfect.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ijtimoiy media hozir boshqacha. Odamlar his-tuyg'ularini baham ko'rishadi. Bu onlaynda.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ijtimoiy media yangi narsa. Odamlar o'z hissiyotlarini onlayn baham ko'rishlari va rasmlarni ko'rsatishlari mumkin. Lekin ba'zida bu haqiqat emas.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ijtimoiy media odamlarning his-tuyg'ularini qanday baham ko'rishini o'zgartirdi.
Masalan, odamlar yaxshi ekanliklarini ko'rsatish uchun xursandchilik rasmlarini joylashtiradilar.
Biroq, ba'zida ular haqiqatan ham baxtli emaslar. Bu boshqa odamlarning o'zlaridan xafa bo'lishiga olib kelishi mumkin. Ijtimoiy media har doim ham haqiqiy hayot emasligini esda tutish muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Ijtimoiy media odamlarning o'z his-tuyg'ularini qanday baham ko'rishiga sezilarli ta'sir ko'rsatdi.
Birinchidan, u tezkor va keng tarqalgan baham ko'rish uchun platforma taqdim etadi.
Biroq, bu o'zini-o'zi tartibga solingan va ko'pincha noreal versiyasini taqdim etishga e'tibor qaratishga olib kelishi mumkin.
Bundan tashqari, internetning anonimligi salbiy xatti-harakatlar va kiberbullingni rag'batlantirishi mumkin, bu esa odamlarning o'z his-tuyg'ularini ochiq va halol baham ko'rishini qiyinlashtiradi.

vocabulary.title: How has...
idioms: air your dirty linen in public - "ko'chada kir yuvish"
sentenceStarters: "Social media has made it..." - "Ijtimoiy media buni qildi..."
"The biggest change is probably..." - "Eng katta o'zgarish, ehtimol..."
"It's had a huge impact on..." - "Bu katta ta'sir ko'rsatdi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Social media has profoundly altered how people share their feelings. Initially, it provided a platform for self-expression, allowing individuals to connect with others who shared similar experiences. However, this has evolved into a more curated and performative display of emotions.

People often present an idealized version of their lives, leading to feelings of inadequacy and comparison among viewers. The pressure to maintain a certain image can also discourage genuine emotional expression. Furthermore, the anonymity afforded by online platforms can embolden people to express negativity or engage in cyberbullying, creating a toxic environment that stifles open and honest communication. It's a double-edged sword. On the one hand, it connects us; on the other hand, it isolates us.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ijtimoiy media odamlarning o'z his-tuyg'ularini baham ko'rish usulini tubdan o'zgartirdi. Dastlab, u o'zini ifoda etish uchun platforma taqdim etdi, bu esa shunga o'xshash tajribalarga ega bo'lgan boshqalar bilan bog'lanish imkonini berdi. Biroq, bu his-tuyg'ularning yanada saralangan va ko'rgazmali namoyishiga aylandi.

Odamlar ko'pincha o'z hayotlarining idealizatsiya qilingan versiyasini taqdim etadilar, bu esa tomoshabinlar orasida yetishmovchilik va taqqoslash tuyg'ulariga olib keladi. Muayyan imidjni saqlash bosimi ham chinakam hissiy ifodani susaytirishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, onlayn platformalar tomonidan taqdim etilgan anonimlik odamlarni salbiylikni ifodalashga yoki kiberbulling bilan shug'ullanishga undashi mumkin, bu esa ochiq va halol muloqotni bo'g'adigan zaharli muhitni yaratadi. Bu ikki tomonlama qilich. Bir tomondan, u bizni bog'laydi; boshqa tomondan, u bizni ajratib qo'yadi.

questions.sampleA1: I no use phone one day. It was quiet. I read book.
questions.sampleA2: I did not use phone. I read a book and went outside. It was good because I was not bored.
questions.sampleB1: Last week, I didn't use my phone for a whole day. It was hard at first, but then it was nice. I read a book and talked to my family. It made me feel more relaxed. For example, I usually check my phone all the time. However, that day I didn't, and it was okay.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so I remember one Sunday last winter when I decided to go completely gadget-free for the whole day — no phone, no laptop, no telly, nothing. To be honest, it started off as a bit of a dare with myself, because I'd noticed I was glued to my screen from morning till night, and I wanted to see if I could actually cope without it. I won't lie, the first hour or two was tough. I kept reaching for my phone out of habit, almost on autopilot. But once I got over that itch, something shifted. I dug out an old novel I'd been meaning to read, went for a long walk in the crisp air, and even cooked a proper lunch from scratch. Time seemed to slow right down, in the best possible way. In terms of my well-being, the break did me the world of good. I felt calmer, more present, and far less frazzled than usual. My head felt clearer, and oddly enough I got more done, because I wasn't constantly sidetracked by notifications pinging away. As for families, I genuinely think carving out some no-screen time is really important. When everyone's buried in their own device, you barely have a proper conversation. Switching off gives you the chance to reconnect, chat over dinner, and actually listen to one another. It sets a good example for kids too, teaching them there's a whole world beyond the screen. At the end of the day, a bit of digital detox now and then does everyone a power of good.

bulletPoints: Describe a time you spent a day without using any electronic gadgets (phone, laptop, etc.).
How did this break affect your mental well-being and productivity?
Why is it important for families to have "no-screen" time in their daily lives?
questions.sampleAnswer:
I remember one weekend I decided to completely disconnect from all electronic gadgets. No phone, no laptop, no TV—nothing. It was a conscious decision because I felt I was spending too much time glued to screens. Initially, it was quite unsettling. I felt this urge to reach for my phone every few minutes, almost like a phantom limb sensation. I didn't realize how addicted I was to constant stimulation.

The break had a profound impact on my mental well-being. I found myself more present in the moment, noticing the details of my surroundings that I usually missed. I read a book, went for a walk in the park, and even tried my hand at gardening. My productivity also increased because I wasn't constantly distracted by notifications and social media. I felt more focused and engaged in the tasks I did undertake. Ultimately, it reduced my stress levels significantly.

“No-screen” time is crucial for families. It encourages face-to-face interaction, fostering stronger bonds and communication skills. It also allows for more creative play and outdoor activities, which are essential for children's development. Moreover, it sets a positive example for children, teaching them to appreciate the world around them and to engage in activities beyond the digital realm. Too much of anything is good for nothing, and that definitely applies to screen time.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Esimda, bir dam olish kunida men barcha elektron qurilmalardan butunlay uzilishga qaror qildim. Na telefon, na noutbuk, na televizor—hech narsa yo'q. Bu ongli qaror edi, chunki men ekranlarga juda ko'p vaqt sarflayotgandek his qildim. Dastlab, bu juda bezovta qiluvchi edi. Har bir necha daqiqada telefonimga qo'l uzatgim kelardi, xuddi xayoliy a'zo sezgisidek. Men doimiy rag'batlantirishga qanchalik o'rganib qolganimni anglamadim.

Bu tanaffus mening ruhiy farovonligimga katta ta'sir ko'rsatdi. Men o'zimni hozirgi lahzada ko'proq his qildim, odatda e'tibor bermaydigan atrofimdagi tafsilotlarni payqadim. Men kitob o'qidim, parkda sayr qildim va hatto bog'dorchilikda ham o'zimni sinab ko'rdim. Mening unumdorligim ham oshdi, chunki meni doimiy ravishda bildirishnomalar va ijtimoiy tarmoqlar chalg'itmasdi. Men o'zimni ko'proq diqqatli va bajarayotgan vazifalarimga jalb qilingandek his qildim. Oxir oqibat, bu mening stress darajamni sezilarli darajada kamaytirdi.

"Ekranlarsiz" vaqt oilalar uchun juda muhim. Bu yuzma-yuz muloqotni rag'batlantiradi, mustahkam aloqalarni va muloqot ko'nikmalarini rivojlantiradi. Shuningdek, u bolalarning rivojlanishi uchun zarur bo'lgan ijodiy o'yin va ochiq havoda mashg'ulotlar uchun imkoniyat yaratadi. Bundan tashqari, u bolalar uchun ijobiy namuna bo'lib, ularga atrofimizdagi dunyoni qadrlashni va raqamli olamdan tashqari faoliyat bilan shug'ullanishni o'rgatadi. Har narsaning me'yori yaxshi, bu ekran vaqtiga ham tegishli.

questions.prompt: All People Should Learn to Cook at Home
questions.sampleA1: Cooking is good. Food is yummy. Some people cook.
questions.sampleA2: Cooking is nice. It is healthy but it takes time. Some people buy food because they are busy.
questions.sampleB1: I think everyone should learn to cook. It is good for your health and saves money. For example, you can make healthy meals at home. However, it can take a lot of time. Some people are too busy to cook.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so the idea that everyone ought to learn to cook at home is one I've got mixed feelings about, though on balance I'm largely in favour. Let me start with the arguments for it. First and foremost, cooking from scratch is far healthier — you know exactly what's going into your food, so you can steer clear of all the salt, sugar and additives you get in takeaways. On top of that, it saves you a small fortune over time, since eating out day in, day out really adds up. And let's not forget, it's a life skill that comes in handy forever; once you've got the hang of it, you're set for life. That said, there's another side to the coin. In today's hectic world, plenty of people are rushed off their feet and simply don't have the time to slave over a hot stove. For others, cooking feels daunting — they lack the confidence and end up burning everything. And to be fair, dining out has its perks too: it's convenient, sociable, and a great way to sample different cuisines. So where do I stand? Personally, I don't think it should be forced on anyone, but I'd strongly encourage everyone to pick up at least the basics. You don't need to be a top chef — just being able to rustle up a simple, healthy meal goes a long way. At the end of the day, cooking is one of those skills that pays off for the rest of your life, so it's well worth the effort.

against: Some people may lack skills or confidence.

questions.sampleAnswer:
The idea that everyone should learn to cook at home is compelling, but it also presents some practical challenges. On the one hand, the arguments in favor are strong. Cooking at home encourages healthier eating habits. You have more control over ingredients, portion sizes, and cooking methods, which can significantly reduce the risk of obesity and related health problems. It also saves money. Eating out regularly can be expensive, while cooking at home allows you to stretch your budget further. Moreover, cooking develops valuable practical skills that can be useful throughout life. It's a skill that keeps on giving.

However, the arguments against are equally valid. Cooking takes time and effort, which many people simply don't have in today's fast-paced world. Some people may lack the skills or confidence to cook, and learning can be daunting. Furthermore, dining out can be more convenient, especially for those with busy schedules or limited kitchen facilities. It also provides an opportunity to socialize and experience different cuisines.

Ultimately, whether or not everyone should learn to cook depends on individual circumstances and priorities. While the benefits of home cooking are undeniable, it's not a one-size-fits-all solution. Perhaps a more realistic goal would be to encourage basic cooking skills and promote awareness of healthy eating habits, rather than mandating that everyone become a home chef. You can lead a horse to water, but you can't make it drink. People need to be motivated to cook.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Hamma uyda ovqat pishirishni o'rganishi kerak degan fikr qiziqarli, lekin u ba'zi amaliy qiyinchiliklarni ham keltirib chiqaradi. Bir tomondan, bu fikrning foydasiga keltiriladigan dalillar kuchli. Uyda ovqat pishirish sog'lom ovqatlanish odatlarini rag'batlantiradi. Sizda ingredientlar, porsiya hajmi va pishirish usullari ustidan ko'proq nazorat bo'ladi, bu esa semizlik va unga bog'liq sog'liq muammolari xavfini sezilarli darajada kamaytirishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, bu pulni tejaydi. Doimiy ravishda tashqarida ovqatlanish qimmatga tushishi mumkin, uyda ovqat pishirish esa byudjetingizni yanada kengaytirishga imkon beradi. Qolaversa, ovqat pishirish hayot davomida foydali bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan qimmatli amaliy ko'nikmalarni rivojlantiradi. Bu doimiy ravishda foyda keltiradigan ko'nikma.

Biroq, qarshi dalillar ham shunchalik asosli. Ovqat pishirish vaqt va kuch talab qiladi, bugungi tez sur'atlar bilan rivojlanayotgan dunyoda ko'pchilikda bu narsa yo'q. Ba'zi odamlarda ovqat pishirish ko'nikmalari yoki ishonchi yetishmasligi mumkin va o'rganish qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, tashqarida ovqatlanish qulayroq bo'lishi mumkin, ayniqsa band jadvalga ega yoki oshxona jihozlari cheklanganlar uchun. Shuningdek, u muloqot qilish va turli xil oshxonalarni tatib ko'rish imkoniyatini beradi.

Oxir oqibat, hamma ovqat pishirishni o'rganishi kerakmi yoki yo'qmi, bu individual sharoitlar va ustuvorliklarga bog'liq. Uyda ovqat pishirishning afzalliklari inkor etib bo'lmas ekan, bu hamma uchun bir xil yechim emas. Ehtimol, yanada real maqsad har bir kishini uy oshpaziga aylantirishdan ko'ra, asosiy ovqat pishirish ko'nikmalarini rag'batlantirish va sog'lom ovqatlanish odatlari haqida xabardorlikni oshirish bo'lar edi. Otni suvga yetaklab borish mumkin, lekin uni ichishga majburlay olmaysiz. Odamlar ovqat pishirishga motivatsiya bo'lishi kerak.
